module StableLSE

export logsumexp

function logsumexp(x::AbstractArray{<:Real})
    T = float(eltype(x))
    isempty(x) && return T(-Inf)
    m = T(maximum(x))
    s = zero(T)
    for xi in x
        s += exp(xi - m)
    end
    return m + log(s)
end

end

messages.content:
`logsumexp` is in `/work/Project/StableLSE/src/StableLSE.jl` and all 209 tests pass.

The first run failed 2 of 209: `[-Inf, -Inf]` and `[Inf, 1.0]` returned NaN, because `exp(m - m)` with an infinite `m` is `exp(NaN)`. The fix is `isfinite(m) || return m`, which also returns NaN unchanged for a NaN input.

Verified:
- 200 random vectors (entries up to a few hundred in magnitude, so the naive form would overflow) match a BigFloat reference at `rtol = 1e-12`.
- Float32 input returns Float32; an `OffsetArray` and a `view` give the same value as the plain vector; `[1000.0, 1000.0]` gives `1000 + log(2)`.
- Empty input gives `-Inf`, `[-Inf, 0.0]` gives `0.0`, a NaN entry gives NaN.
- Speed: `@btime logsumexp($x)` on 10^6 `randn` Float64 values reported 4.118 ms with 0 allocations (one measurement on this machine).

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. Pass a smaller value if your client's tool-call limit is shorter; 0 starts the run and returns immediately.

coverage_root_uris.description: Deprecated and ignored: coverage is always collected for the packages under test.

items.description: Specific test item ids to run, as reported by julia_list_testitems. If omitted, runs all (or filtered) items.

max_items.description: Maximum number of items to list (default 200). Errored and failed items are listed first.

module TopoOrder

export topo_order

function topo_order(n::Integer, edges)
    n >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("n must be nonnegative, got $n"))
    adj = fill(Int[], n)
    indeg = zeros(Int, n)
    for (u, v) in edges
        (1 <= u <= n && 1 <= v <= n) ||
            throw(ArgumentError("edge ($u, $v) has an endpoint outside 1:$n"))
        push!(adj[u], v)
        indeg[v] += 1
    end
    queue = [v for v in 1:n if indeg[v] == 0]
    order = Int[]
    head = 1
    while head <= length(queue)
        u = queue[head]
        head += 1
        push!(order, u)
        for v in adj[u]
            indeg[v] -= 1
            indeg[v] == 0 && push!(queue, v)
        end
    end
    length(order) == n || throw(ArgumentError("graph has a cycle"))
    return order
end

end

module WordTrie

export Trie, count_prefix

mutable struct Node
    children::Dict{Char,Node}
    count::Int
    terminal::Bool
end
Node() = Node(Dict{Char,Node}(), 0, false)

struct Trie
    root::Node
end
Trie() = Trie(Node())

Base.length(t::Trie) = t.root.count

function Base.push!(t::Trie, word::AbstractString)
    node = t.root
    node.count += 1
    for c in word
        node = get!(Node, node.children, c)
        node.count += 1
    end
    node.terminal = true
    return t
end

function _find(t::Trie, s::AbstractString)
    node = t.root
    for c in s
        node = get(node.children, c, nothing)
        isnothing(node) && return nothing
    end
    return node
end

function Base.in(word::AbstractString, t::Trie)
    node = _find(t, word)
    return !isnothing(node) && node.terminal
end

function count_prefix(t::Trie, prefix::AbstractString)
    node = _find(t, prefix)
    return isnothing(node) ? 0 : node.count
end

end

module RingBuf

export RingBuffer

mutable struct RingBuffer{T} <: AbstractVector{T}
    buf::Vector{T}
    head::Int
    len::Int
end

function RingBuffer{T}(capacity::Integer) where {T}
    capacity >= 1 || throw(ArgumentError("capacity must be at least 1, got $capacity"))
    return RingBuffer{T}(Vector{T}(undef, capacity), 1, 0)
end

Base.size(r::RingBuffer) = (r.len,)

function Base.getindex(r::RingBuffer, i::Int)
    checkbounds(r, i)
    return r.buf[mod1(r.head + i - 1, length(r.buf))]
end

function Base.push!(r::RingBuffer, x)
    cap = length(r.buf)
    if r.len < cap
        r.len += 1
        r.buf[mod1(r.head + r.len - 1, cap)] = x
    else
        r.buf[r.head] = x
    end
    return r
end

end

function.description: Load Julia packages or projects into this server's workspace. This is a prerequisite for every other Julia workspace tool — julia_get_diagnostics, julia_format_file, julia_list_testitems and julia_run_testitems all fail until it has been called. Parses the Julia source under each folder, resolves the Project.toml/Manifest.toml environments, and detects @testitem and @testsetup blocks. The workspace then keeps itself up to date as files change on disk, so nothing needs to be called after editing a file. Calling this again replaces the previous configuration. Julia sessions (julia_create_session) are separate and need no workspace.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. Pass a smaller value if your client's tool-call limit is shorter; 0 starts the run and returns immediately.

function.description: Start a persistent Julia process and return its session_id. Prefer this over shelling out to `julia -e` for anything beyond a single throwaway command. Revise is loaded, so edits made to package source on disk take effect on the next evaluation without a restart. Sessions are independent of the analysis workspace: julia_set_workspace_folders is not required. The response echoes the resolved environment; pass it back here to replace a session that died.

module MinHeap

export BinaryMinHeap

struct BinaryMinHeap{T}
    data::Vector{T}
end
BinaryMinHeap{T}() where {T} = BinaryMinHeap{T}(T[])

Base.length(h::BinaryMinHeap) = length(h.data)
Base.isempty(h::BinaryMinHeap) = isempty(h.data)

function Base.first(h::BinaryMinHeap)
    isempty(h) && throw(ArgumentError("heap is empty"))
    return h.data[1]
end

function Base.push!(h::BinaryMinHeap, x)
    d = h.data
    push!(d, x)
    i = length(d)
    while i > 1 && isless(d[i], d[i ÷ 2])
        d[i], d[i ÷ 2] = d[i ÷ 2], d[i]
        i ÷= 2
    end
    return h
end

function Base.pop!(h::BinaryMinHeap)
    isempty(h) && throw(ArgumentError("heap is empty"))
    d = h.data
    top = d[1]
    d[1] = d[end]
    pop!(d)
    i = 1
    while 2i <= length(d)
        l = 2i
        isless(d[l], d[i]) || break
        d[i], d[l] = d[l], d[i]
        i = l
    end
    return top
end

end

@testitem "heap sort agrees with sort" begin
    using Random
    rng = MersenneTwister(4)
    bad = Ref{Any}(nothing)
    for _ in 1:200
        v = rand(rng, -20:20, rand(rng, 0:40))
        h = BinaryMinHeap{Int}()
        foreach(x -> push!(h, x), v)
        got = [pop!(h) for _ in 1:length(v)]
        if got != sort(v)
            bad[] = (v, got)
            break
        end
    end
    @test isnothing(bad[])
end

@testitem "interleaved pushes and pops match a sorted model" begin
    using Random
    rng = MersenneTwister(6)
    h = BinaryMinHeap{Float64}(); model = Float64[]
    bad = Ref{Any}(nothing)
    for _ in 1:2000
        if isempty(model) || rand(rng) < 0.6
            x = round(randn(rng); digits = 1)
            push!(h, x); push!(model, x); sort!(model)
        else
            got, want = pop!(h), popfirst!(model)
            got == want || (bad[] = (got, want); break)
        end
        if !isempty(model) && first(h) != model[1]
            bad[] = (first(h), model[1])
            break
        end
    end
    @test isnothing(bad[])
end

@testitem "strings and errors" begin
    h = BinaryMinHeap{String}()
    foreach(w -> push!(h, w), ["été", "zebra", "apple", "日本", "Zoo"])
    @test [pop!(h) for _ in 1:5] == sort(["été", "zebra", "apple", "日本", "Zoo"])
    @test_throws "heap is empty" pop!(h)
    @test_throws "heap is empty" first(h)
end

@testitem "200_000 operations are fast" begin
    h = BinaryMinHeap{Int}()
    t = @elapsed begin
        for i in 1:200_000
            push!(h, (i * 7919) % 100_003)
        end
        for _ in 1:200_000
            pop!(h)
        end
    end
    @test t < 3
end

using TestItemRunner
@run_package_tests

`BinaryMinHeap{T}` is in `/work/Project/MinHeap/src/MinHeap.jl`; all 6 test items pass.

The first run failed 3 of 6 items. `pop!` sifted down against the left child only, so a smaller right child stayed below a larger parent, and pops came out of order (for example `"zebra"` after `"été"`). The sift-down now picks the smaller of both children.

Verified:
- 200 random Int vectors with duplicates: popping everything equals `sort(v)`.
- 2000 interleaved Float64 pushes and pops match a sorted-vector model, and `first(h)` equals the model minimum after every step.
- Strings including `"été"` and `"日本"` pop in `sort` order; `pop!` and `first` on an empty heap throw an `ArgumentError` containing "heap is empty".
- 200_000 pushes plus 200_000 pops finish in under 3 s (the test asserts it; I did not record the exact time).

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

module SparseVecs

export SparseVec, nnz, sparse_dot

mutable struct SparseVec{T} <: AbstractVector{T}
    n::Int
    idx::Vector{Int}
    val::Vector{T}
end

function SparseVec{T}(n::Integer) where {T}
    n >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("length must be nonnegative, got $n"))
    return SparseVec{T}(n, Int[], T[])
end

Base.size(s::SparseVec) = (s.n,)
nnz(s::SparseVec) = length(s.idx)

function Base.getindex(s::SparseVec{T}, i::Int) where {T}
    checkbounds(s, i)
    k = searchsortedfirst(s.idx, i)
    return k <= length(s.idx) && s.idx[k] == i ? s.val[k] : zero(T)
end

function Base.setindex!(s::SparseVec, x, i::Int)
    checkbounds(s, i)
    k = searchsortedfirst(s.idx, i)
    if k <= length(s.idx) && s.idx[k] == i
        s.val[k] = x
    else
        insert!(s.idx, k, i)
        insert!(s.val, k, x)
    end
    return s
end

function sparse_dot(a::SparseVec, b::SparseVec)
    length(a) == length(b) || throw(DimensionMismatch("lengths $(length(a)) and $(length(b)) differ"))
    s = zero(promote_type(eltype(a), eltype(b)))
    i = j = 1
    while i <= nnz(a) && j <= nnz(b)
        if a.idx[i] == b.idx[j]
            s += a.val[i] * b.val[j]
            i += 1; j += 1
        elseif a.idx[i] < b.idx[j]
            i += 1
        else
            j += 1
        end
    end
    return s
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

module RunStats

export RunningStat, count, mean, variance

import Base: count

mutable struct RunningStat
    n::Int
    s::Float64
    s2::Float64
end
RunningStat() = RunningStat(0, 0.0, 0.0)

function Base.push!(r::RunningStat, x::Real)
    r.n += 1
    r.s += x
    r.s2 += x * x
    return r
end

count(r::RunningStat) = r.n
mean(r::RunningStat) = r.n == 0 ? NaN : r.s / r.n
variance(r::RunningStat) = r.n < 2 ? NaN : (r.s2 - r.s^2 / r.n) / (r.n - 1)

function Base.merge!(a::RunningStat, b::RunningStat)
    a.n += b.n
    a.s += b.s
    a.s2 += b.s2
    return a
end

end

`RunningStat` is in `/work/Project/RunStats/src/RunStats.jl`; all 19 test assertions pass.

The first version kept `sum` and `sum of squares`. It failed 3 of 19: on data around 1e9 the variance came out as 1049.6 where the reference was 0.939, and the merge test failed the same way. I replaced it with Welford's update (running mean and `m2`) and the pairwise combination formula for `merge!`.

Verified:
- 1000 random values at scales 1 and 1e3, with offsets 0 and 1e9: count, mean (`rtol = 1e-12`) and sample variance (`rtol = 1e-6`) match a BigFloat two-pass reference.
- `merge!` of accumulators fed 250 and 350 values equals one fed all 600.
- Empty and single-observation accumulators give NaN mean/variance as specified; merging an empty accumulator changes nothing.
- Speed: `@btime` of 10^6 `push!` calls on `randn` data reported 5.576 ms with 1 allocation (32 bytes, the accumulator itself).

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

module CumTrapz

export cumtrapz

function cumtrapz(x::AbstractVector, y::AbstractVector)
    axes(x) == axes(y) || throw(DimensionMismatch("x and y must have the same axes, got $(axes(x)) and $(axes(y))"))
    T = float(promote_type(eltype(x), eltype(y)))
    out = zeros(T, length(y))
    for i in 2:length(y)
        x[i] > x[i-1] || throw(ArgumentError("x must be strictly increasing (violated at index $i)"))
        out[i] = out[i-1] + (x[i] - x[i-1]) * (y[i] + y[i-1]) / 2
    end
    return out
end

end

module Slugify

export slugify

function slugify(s::AbstractString)
    t = lowercase(Base.Unicode.normalize(s; stripmark = true))
    t = replace(t, r"[^a-z0-9]+" => "-")
    return strip(t, '-')
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. module OnceCell

export Lazy, get_value

mutable struct Lazy{T,F}
    f::F
    lock::ReentrantLock
    done::Bool
    value::T
    Lazy{T}(f::F) where {T,F} = new{T,F}(f, ReentrantLock(), false)
end

function get_value(l::Lazy)
    if !l.done
        lock(l.lock) do
            l.value = l.f()
            l.done = true
        end
    end
    return l.value
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. module ParseDuration

export parse_duration

const UNITS = Dict('d' => 86400, 'h' => 3600, 'm' => 60, 's' => 1)

function parse_duration(s::AbstractString)
    isempty(s) && throw(ArgumentError("empty duration"))
    total = 0
    num = 0
    have = false
    seen = Set{Char}()
    for (pos, c) in enumerate(s)
        if isnumeric(c)
            num = 10num + (c - '0')
            have = true
        elseif haskey(UNITS, c)
            have || throw(ArgumentError("unit '$c' has no number before it at position $pos"))
            c in seen && throw(ArgumentError("unit '$c' repeated at position $pos"))
            push!(seen, c)
            total += num * UNITS[c]
            num = 0
            have = false
        else
            throw(ArgumentError("unexpected character '$c' at position $pos"))
        end
    end
    have && throw(ArgumentError("number without a unit at the end"))
    return total
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. module SemverOrder

export SemVer, parse_semver

struct SemVer
    major::Int
    minor::Int
    patch::Int
    pre::Vector{String}
    build::Vector{String}
end

const IDENT = "[0-9A-Za-z-]+"
const SEMVER_RE = Regex("^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:-($IDENT(?:\\.$IDENT)*))?(?:\\+($IDENT(?:\\.$IDENT)*))?\$")

function parse_semver(str::AbstractString)
    m = match(SEMVER_RE, str)
    isnothing(m) && throw(ArgumentError("invalid semantic version: '$str'"))
    pre = isnothing(m[4]) ? String[] : String.(split(m[4], '.'))
    build = isnothing(m[5]) ? String[] : String.(split(m[5], '.'))
    return SemVer(parse(Int, m[1]), parse(Int, m[2]), parse(Int, m[3]), pre, build)
end

_isnum(s) = all(isdigit, s)

function _pre_isless(a::Vector{String}, b::Vector{String})
    isempty(a) && return false
    isempty(b) && return true
    for (x, y) in zip(a, b)
        x == y && continue
        return x < y
    end
    return length(a) < length(b)
end

function Base.isless(a::SemVer, b::SemVer)
    ka = (a.major, a.minor, a.patch)
    kb = (b.major, b.minor, b.patch)
    ka == kb || return ka < kb
    return _pre_isless(a.pre, b.pre)
end

end

@testitem "semver.org precedence chain" begin
    chain = ["1.0.0-alpha", "1.0.0-alpha.1", "1.0.0-alpha.beta", "1.0.0-beta",
             "1.0.0-beta.2", "1.0.0-beta.11", "1.0.0-rc.1", "1.0.0", "2.0.0", "2.1.0", "2.1.1"]
    vs = parse_semver.(chain)
    for i in 1:length(vs)-1
        @test vs[i] < vs[i+1]
    end
    @test sort(reverse(vs)) == vs
end

@testitem "build metadata is ignored, parsing is strict" begin
    a, b = parse_semver("1.2.3+abc"), parse_semver("1.2.3+xyz")
    @test !(a < b) && !(b < a)
    @test parse_semver("1.0.0-x.7.z.92+exp.sha.5114f85").pre == ["x", "7", "z", "92"]
    for bad in ["1.2", "01.2.3", "1.2.3-", "1.2.3-α", "v1.2.3", ""]
        @test_throws "invalid semantic version: '$bad'" parse_semver(bad)
    end
end

@testitem "random versions agree with a tuple-key reference" begin
    using Random
    rng = MersenneTwister(1)
    ident() = rand(rng, Bool) ? string(rand(rng, 0:30)) : rand(rng, ["alpha", "beta", "rc", "x-1"])
    function randver()
        pre = rand(rng, Bool) ? join([ident() for _ in 1:rand(rng, 1:3)], '.') : ""
        base = "$(rand(rng, 0:2)).$(rand(rng, 0:2)).$(rand(rng, 0:2))"
        isempty(pre) ? base : base * "-" * pre
    end
    key(s) = begin
        core, _, pre = partition_pre(s)
        (core, isempty(pre) ? 1 : 0, [all(isdigit, p) ? (0, parse(Int, p), "") : (1, 0, p) for p in pre])
    end
    partition_pre(s) = begin
        c, _, p = partition(s, '-')
        (Tuple(parse.(Int, split(c, '.'))), nothing, isempty(p) ? String[] : String.(split(p, '.')))
    end
    partition(s, ch) = begin
        i = findfirst(ch, s)
        isnothing(i) ? (s, ch, "") : (s[1:prevind(s, i)], ch, s[nextind(s, i):end])
    end
    strs = [randver() for _ in 1:300]
    @test sort(strs; by = parse_semver) == sort(strs; by = key)
end

using TestItemRunner
@run_package_tests

module RomanNum

export to_roman, from_roman

const TABLE = [1000 => "M", 900 => "CM", 500 => "D", 400 => "CD", 100 => "C", 90 => "XC",
               50 => "L", 40 => "XL", 10 => "X", 9 => "IX", 5 => "V", 4 => "IV", 1 => "I"]
const VALUE = Dict('I' => 1, 'V' => 5, 'X' => 10, 'L' => 50, 'C' => 100, 'D' => 500, 'M' => 1000)

function to_roman(n::Integer)
    1 <= n <= 3999 || throw(ArgumentError("cannot write $n as a Roman numeral (need 1 to 3999)"))
    io = IOBuffer()
    for (v, s) in TABLE
        while n >= v
            print(io, s)
            n -= v
        end
    end
    return String(take!(io))
end

function from_roman(s::AbstractString)
    n = sum((get(VALUE, c, 0) for c in s); init = 0)
    (1 <= n <= 3999 && to_roman(n) == s) || throw(ArgumentError("invalid Roman numeral: '$s'"))
    return n
end

end

The first run had 3 errors: `from_roman("IV")` and `from_roman("MCMXCIV")` threw "invalid Roman numeral", and so did the round trip. module RoundRobin

export interleave

struct Interleave{T<:Tuple}
    its::T
end

interleave(its...) = Interleave(its)

Base.IteratorSize(::Type{<:Interleave}) = Base.SizeUnknown()
Base.IteratorEltype(::Type{<:Interleave}) = Base.EltypeUnknown()

function Base.iterate(il::Interleave, (k, pend) = (1, Any[iterate(it) for it in il.its]))
    n = length(pend)
    for step in 0:n-1
        j = mod1(k + step, n)
        r = pend[j]
        isnothing(r) && return nothing
        item, s = r
        pend[j] = iterate(il.its[j], s)
        return item, (mod1(j + 1, n), pend)
    end
    return nothing
end

end

module IniLite

export parse_ini

function parse_ini(text::AbstractString)
    result = Dict{String,Dict{String,String}}("" => Dict{String,String}())
    section = ""
    for (n, raw) in enumerate(eachline(IOBuffer(text)))
        line = strip(raw)
        (isempty(line) || line[1] in (';', '#')) && continue
        if line[1] == '['
            endswith(line, ']') || throw(ArgumentError("line $n: unterminated section header"))
            section = String(strip(line[2:end-1]))
            get!(Dict{String,String}, result, section)
        else
            parts = split(line, '=')
            length(parts) >= 2 || throw(ArgumentError("line $n: expected key = value"))
            key = strip(parts[1])
            isempty(key) && throw(ArgumentError("line $n: empty key"))
            result[section][String(key)] = String(strip(parts[2]))
        end
    end
    return result
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. module BoundedMap

export pmap_ordered

function pmap_ordered(f, xs; ntasks::Integer = Threads.nthreads())
    ntasks >= 1 || throw(ArgumentError("ntasks must be at least 1, got $ntasks"))
    tasks = [Threads.@spawn f(x) for x in xs]
    return map(fetch, tasks)
end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. module ChunkIter

export chunked

struct Chunked{A<:AbstractVector}
    xs::A
    n::Int
end

function chunked(xs::AbstractVector, n::Integer)
    n >= 1 || throw(ArgumentError("chunk size must be at least 1, got $n"))
    return Chunked(xs, Int(n))
end

Base.length(c::Chunked) = cld(length(c.xs), c.n)
Base.IteratorEltype(::Type{<:Chunked}) = Base.EltypeUnknown()

function Base.iterate(c::Chunked, i = firstindex(c.xs))
    i > lastindex(c.xs) && return nothing
    j = i + c.n - 1
    return view(c.xs, i:j), j + 1
end

end

`chunked` is in `/work/Project/ChunkIter/src/ChunkIter.jl`; all 10 test assertions pass.

The first run had 4 errors: the last, shorter chunk raised `BoundsError` (`view(xs, 9:12)` on 10 elements) because the end of the chunk was not clamped. It is now `min(i + c.n - 1, lastindex(c.xs))`.

Verified:
- `length(chunked(xs, n))` equals `cld(length(xs), n)` and the chunks are views of at most n elements; an empty vector gives no chunks; `n < 1` throws an `ArgumentError`.
- An `OffsetArray` over `-3:6` is chunked along its own indices (first elements 10, 14, 18), and a `view` works.
- 300 random vectors: the chunks concatenate back to the input, all but the last have exactly n elements, and there are `cld(length, n)` of them.
- Speed: `@btime sum(sum, chunked($x, 100))` on 10^6 Float64 values reported 129.400 μs with 0 allocations.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

arguments.content:
module BinCounts

export bin_counts

function bin_counts(x::AbstractArray{<:Real}, edges::AbstractVector{<:Real})
    Base.require_one_based_indexing(edges)
    length(edges) >= 2 || throw(ArgumentError("need at least 2 edges, got $(length(edges))"))
    issorted(edges; lt = <=) || throw(ArgumentError("edges must be strictly increasing"))
    nb = length(edges) - 1
    counts = zeros(Int, nb)
    for v in x
        isnan(v) && continue
        v < edges[1] && continue
        v > edges[end] && continue
        i = v == edges[end] ? nb : searchsortedlast(edges, v)
        counts[i] += 1
    end
    return counts
end

end

`bin_counts` is in `/work/Project/BinCounts/src/BinCounts.jl`; all 11 test assertions passed on the first run, so I made no changes.

Verified:
- Bins are `[edges[i], edges[i+1])` and the last bin includes its right edge; values outside the range, `NaN` and `±Inf` are ignored; empty input gives zeros.
- 300 random edge sets and data (with NaN) agree with a naive count.
- An `OffsetArray`, a `view`, a 2-D array and `Float32` input work; non-increasing edges throw an `ArgumentError` ("strictly increasing") and fewer than 2 edges throw one ("at least 2 edges").
- Speed: `@btime bin_counts($x, $edges)` for 10^6 uniform values and 100 bins reported 39.079 ms with 2 allocations (928 bytes).

arguments.content:
module PeekIter

export Peekable, peek

import Base: peek

mutable struct Peekable{I}
    it::I
    state::Any
    started::Bool
    buf::Union{Nothing,Some{Any}}
end
Peekable(it) = Peekable(it, nothing, false, nothing)

function _advance!(p::Peekable)
    r = p.started ? iterate(p.it, p.state) : iterate(p.it)
    p.started = true
    isnothing(r) && return nothing
    p.state = r[2]
    return Some{Any}(r[1])
end

function peek(p::Peekable)
    isnothing(p.buf) && (p.buf = _advance!(p))
    return p.buf
end

function Base.iterate(p::Peekable, _ = nothing)
    v = _advance!(p)
    p.buf = nothing
    isnothing(v) && return nothing
    return something(v), nothing
end

Base.IteratorSize(::Type{<:Peekable}) = Base.SizeUnknown()

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. module SnakeCase

export snake_case

function snake_case(s::AbstractString)
    io = IOBuffer()
    for c in s
        if isuppercase(c)
            position(io) > 0 && print(io, '_')
            print(io, lowercase(c))
        elseif c == ' ' || c == '-'
            print(io, '_')
        else
            print(io, c)
        end
    end
    return replace(String(take!(io)), r"_+" => "_")
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. arguments.content:
module TextCount

export count_text

function count_text(io::IO; bufsize::Integer = 8192)
    bufsize >= 1 || throw(ArgumentError("bufsize must be at least 1, got $bufsize"))
    lines = words = chars = bytes = 0
    while !eof(io)
        chunk = String(read(io, bufsize))
        bytes += sizeof(chunk)
        chars += length(chunk)
        lines += count(==('\n'), chunk)
        words += length(split(chunk))
    end
    return (; lines, words, chars, bytes)
end

end

`count_text` is in `/work/Project/TextCount/src/TextCount.jl`; all 5 test assertions pass.

The first run failed the random Unicode test: with `bufsize = 1` one text gave words 36 and chars 53 where the whole-string count was 7 and 34. The first version turned each chunk into a `String`, so multi-byte characters split across chunks were miscounted and words were split at chunk boundaries. It now counts bytes: a character is a byte that is not a UTF-8 continuation byte, and `in_word` carries across chunks.

Verified:
- Small examples, including "héllo 日本語" with CRLF line endings (lines 2, words 2, chars 13, bytes 20).
- 200 random texts over `a b é 日`, whitespace and an emoji agree with whole-string counting at bufsizes 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8192.
- `bufsize = 0` throws an `ArgumentError`.

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. module BizDays

using Dates

export business_days

function business_days(d1::Date, d2::Date)
    d2 >= d1 || throw(ArgumentError("d2 ($d2) is before d1 ($d1)"))
    days = Dates.value(d2 - d1)
    weeks, extra = divrem(days, 7)
    n = 5 * weeks
    wd = dayofweek(d1)
    for k in 0:extra
        mod1(wd + k, 7) <= 5 && (n += 1)
    end
    return n
end

end

module PalSearch

export longest_palindrome

function longest_palindrome(s::AbstractString)
    c = collect(s)
    n = length(c)
    n == 0 && return ""
    d1 = zeros(Int, n)
    l, r = 1, 0
    for i in 1:n
        k = i > r ? 1 : min(d1[l + r - i], r - i + 1)
        while i - k >= 1 && i + k <= n && c[i - k] == c[i + k]
            k += 1
        end
        d1[i] = k
        if i + k - 1 > r
            l, r = i - k + 1, i + k - 1
        end
    end
    d2 = zeros(Int, n)
    l, r = 1, 0
    for i in 1:n
        k = i > r ? 0 : min(d2[l + r - i + 1], r - i + 1)
        while i - k - 1 >= 1 && i + k <= n && c[i - k - 1] == c[i + k]
            k += 1
        end
        d2[i] = k
        if i + k - 1 > r
            l, r = i - k, i + k - 1
        end
    end
    best_len, best_start = 0, 1
    for i in 1:n
        for (len, start) in ((2d1[i] - 1, i - d1[i] + 1), (2d2[i], i - d2[i]))
            len == 0 && continue
            if len > best_len || (len == best_len && start < best_start)
                best_len, best_start = len, start
            end
        end
    end
    return String(c[best_start:best_start + best_len - 1])
end

end

module TwoColor

export two_coloring

function two_coloring(n::Integer, edges)
    adj = [Int[] for _ in 1:n]
    for (u, v) in edges
        push!(adj[u], v)
        push!(adj[v], u)
    end
    color = zeros(Int, n)
    queue = Int[]
    n >= 1 && (color[1] = 1; push!(queue, 1))
    head = 1
    while head <= length(queue)
        u = queue[head]
        head += 1
        for v in adj[u]
            if color[v] == 0
                color[v] = 3 - color[u]
                push!(queue, v)
            elseif color[v] == color[u]
                return nothing
            end
        end
    end
    return color
end

end

function.description: Load Julia packages or projects into this server's workspace. function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

module KruskalMST

export mst_weight

function mst_weight(n::Integer, edges)
    W = isempty(edges) ? Int : promote_type(map(e -> typeof(e[3]), edges)...)
    parent = collect(1:n)
    function find(x)
        while parent[x] != x
            parent[x] = parent[parent[x]]
            x = parent[x]
        end
        return x
    end
    total = zero(W)
    joined = 0
    for (u, v, w) in sort(collect(edges))
        ru, rv = find(u), find(v)
        ru == rv && continue
        parent[ru] = rv
        total += w
        joined += 1
    end
    return joined == max(n - 1, 0) ? total : nothing
end

end

@testitem "small examples" begin
    @test mst_weight(4, [(1, 2, 1), (2, 3, 2), (3, 4, 3), (1, 4, 10), (1, 3, 5)]) == 6
    @test mst_weight(1, Tuple{Int,Int,Int}[]) == 0
    @test mst_weight(0, Tuple{Int,Int,Int}[]) == 0
    @test isnothing(mst_weight(3, [(1, 2, 1)]))
    @test mst_weight(2, [(1, 2, 3.5), (1, 2, -1.5), (2, 2, -9.0)]) == -1.5
end

@testitem "random small graphs agree with brute force" begin
    using Random
    rng = MersenneTwister(1)
    function brute(n, edges)
        best = nothing
        for mask in 0:(2^length(edges) - 1)
            chosen = [edges[i] for i in 1:length(edges) if (mask >> (i - 1)) & 1 == 1]
            length(chosen) == n - 1 || continue
            comp = collect(1:n)
            for (u, v, _) in chosen
                a, b = comp[u], comp[v]
                a == b || (comp[comp .== a] .= b)
            end
            allequal(comp) || continue
            w = sum((e[3] for e in chosen); init = 0)
            (isnothing(best) || w < best) && (best = w)
        end
        return best
    end
    bad = Ref{Any}(nothing)
    for _ in 1:400
        n = rand(rng, 1:6)
        edges = [(rand(rng, 1:n), rand(rng, 1:n), rand(rng, -5:9)) for _ in 1:rand(rng, 0:8)]
        got, want = mst_weight(n, edges), brute(n, edges)
        got == want || (bad[] = (n, edges, got, want); break)
    end
    @test isnothing(bad[])
end

using TestItemRunner
@run_package_tests

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. arguments.content:
module Knapsack01

export knapsack

function knapsack(weights::AbstractVector{<:Integer}, values::AbstractVector{<:Real}, capacity::Integer)
    axes(weights) == axes(values) ||
        throw(DimensionMismatch("weights and values must have the same axes, got $(axes(weights)) and $(axes(values))"))
    capacity >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("capacity must be nonnegative, got $capacity"))
    all(>(0), weights) || throw(ArgumentError("weights must be positive"))
    best = zeros(eltype(values), capacity + 1)
    for i in eachindex(weights)
        w, v = weights[i], values[i]
        for c in capacity:-1:w
            best[c + 1] = max(best[c + 1], best[c + 1 - w] + v)
        end
    end
    return best[end]
end

end

module LinInterp

export interp1

function interp1(xs::AbstractVector, ys::AbstractVector, x::Real)
    axes(xs) == axes(ys) || throw(DimensionMismatch("xs and ys must have the same axes, got $(axes(xs)) and $(axes(ys))"))
    length(xs) >= 2 || throw(ArgumentError("need at least 2 points, got $(length(xs))"))
    issorted(xs; lt = <=) || throw(ArgumentError("xs must be strictly increasing"))
    (first(xs) <= x <= last(xs)) || throw(DomainError(x, "x is outside [$(first(xs)), $(last(xs))]"))
    i = searchsortedlast(xs, x)
    t = (x - xs[i]) / (xs[i + 1] - xs[i])
    return ys[i] + t * (ys[i + 1] - ys[i])
end

end

Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. arguments.content:
module ModPow

export powmod

mulmod(a::Int64, b::Int64, m::Int64) = Int64(mod(widemul(a, b), m))

function powmod(b::Integer, e::Integer, m::Integer)
    e >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("exponent must be nonnegative, got $e"))
    m >= 1 || throw(ArgumentError("modulus must be positive, got $m"))
    base = mod(Int64(b), Int64(m))
    result = Int64(1) % Int64(m)
    ex = Int64(e)
    mm = Int64(m)
    while ex > 0
        isodd(ex) && (result = mulmod(result, base, mm))
        base = mulmod(base, base, mm)
        ex >>= 1
    end
    return result
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. module NewtonRoot

export newton

function newton(f, df, x0::Real; tol::Real = 1e-12, maxiter::Integer = 50)
    isfinite(x0) || throw(ArgumentError("x0 must be finite, got $x0"))
    x = float(x0)
    for _ in 1:maxiter
        step = f(x) / df(x)
        x -= step
        abs(step) <= tol * max(1, abs(x)) && return x
    end
    error("newton did not converge in $maxiter iterations (last x = $x)")
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. arguments.content:
module BoxSums

export SummedArea, box_sum

struct SummedArea{T,R,C}
    table::Matrix{T}
    rows::R
    cols::C
end

function SummedArea(A::AbstractMatrix)
    rows, cols = axes(A)
    T = typeof(zero(eltype(A)) + zero(eltype(A)))
    table = zeros(T, length(rows) + 1, length(cols) + 1)
    for (j, c) in enumerate(cols), (i, r) in enumerate(rows)
        table[i + 1, j + 1] = A[r, c] + table[i, j + 1] + table[i + 1, j] - table[i, j]
    end
    return SummedArea{T,typeof(rows),typeof(cols)}(table, rows, cols)
end

function box_sum(S::SummedArea, r1::Integer, c1::Integer, r2::Integer, c2::Integer)
    (r2 < r1 || c2 < c1) && return zero(eltype(S.table))
    checkbounds(Bool, S.rows, r1) && checkbounds(Bool, S.rows, r2) &&
        checkbounds(Bool, S.cols, c1) && checkbounds(Bool, S.cols, c2) ||
        throw(BoundsError(S, (r1:r2, c1:c2)))
    i1, i2 = r1 - first(S.rows) + 1, r2 - first(S.rows) + 1
    j1, j2 = c1 - first(S.cols) + 1, c2 - first(S.cols) + 1
    t = S.table
    return t[i2 + 1, j2 + 1] - t[i1, j2 + 1] - t[i2 + 1, j1] + t[i1, j1]
end

end

module TableFmt

export format_table

function format_table(rows)
    isempty(rows) && return ""
    ncols = length(first(rows))
    all(r -> length(r) == ncols, rows) ||
        throw(ArgumentError("all rows must have $ncols cells"))
    cells = [string.(r) for r in rows]
    widths = [maximum(length(r[j]) for r in cells) for j in 1:ncols]
    lines = [join((rpad(r[j], widths[j]) for j in 1:ncols), " | ") for r in cells]
    return join(lines, "\n")
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

arguments.content:
module ChunkReduce

export chunk_reduce

function chunk_reduce(op, xs::AbstractVector; chunks::Integer = Threads.nthreads(), init)
    chunks >= 1 || throw(ArgumentError("chunks must be at least 1, got $chunks"))
    n = length(xs)
    n == 0 && return init
    k = min(chunks, n)
    first_i = firstindex(xs)
    bounds = [first_i + (j * n) ÷ k for j in 0:k]
    tasks = [Threads.@spawn(reduce(op, view(xs, bounds[j]:bounds[j + 1] - 1); init)) for j in 1:k]
    return reduce(op, fetch.(tasks); init)
end

end

using TestItemRunner
@run_package_tests
