function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

module QueryParse

export parse_query, encode_component

function decode_component(s::AbstractString)
    out = IOBuffer()
    i = firstindex(s)
    while i <= lastindex(s)
        c = s[i]
        if c == '+'
            print(out, ' ')
        elseif c == '%'
            hex = SubString(s, nextind(s, i), min(lastindex(s), nextind(s, i, 2)))
            length(hex) == 2 && all(isxdigit, hex) ||
                throw(ArgumentError("malformed percent escape in '$s'"))
            print(out, Char(parse(UInt8, hex; base = 16)))
            i = nextind(s, i, 2)
        else
            print(out, c)
        end
        i = nextind(s, i)
    end
    return String(take!(out))
end

function parse_query(s::AbstractString)
    result = Dict{String,Vector{String}}()
    for piece in split(s, '&'; keepempty = false)
        k, v = occursin('=', piece) ? split(piece, '='; limit = 2) : (piece, "")
        push!(get!(Vector{String}, result, decode_component(k)), decode_component(v))
    end
    return result
end

function encode_component(s::AbstractString)
    out = IOBuffer()
    for b in codeunits(s)
        c = Char(b)
        if isascii(c) && (isletter(c) || isdigit(c) || c in "-_.~")
            print(out, c)
        else
            print(out, '%', uppercase(string(b, base = 16, pad = 2)))
        end
    end
    return String(take!(out))
end

end

module TallyCount

export Counter, add!, remove!, total, most_common

struct Counter{K}
    counts::Dict{K,Int}
end
Counter{K}() where {K} = Counter{K}(Dict{K,Int}())

Base.length(c::Counter) = length(c.counts)
Base.getindex(c::Counter, key) = get(c.counts, key, 0)
total(c::Counter) = sum(values(c.counts); init = 0)

function add!(c::Counter, key, n::Integer = 1)
    n >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("cannot add a negative count ($n); use remove!"))
    n == 0 && return c
    c.counts[key] = get(c.counts, key, 0) + n
    return c
end

function remove!(c::Counter, key, n::Integer = 1)
    n >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("cannot remove a negative count ($n); use add!"))
    have = c[key]
    have >= n || throw(ArgumentError("cannot remove $n of $(repr(key)): only $have present"))
    if have == n
        delete!(c.counts, key)
    else
        c.counts[key] = have - n
    end
    return c
end

function most_common(c::Counter, k::Integer)
    k >= 0 || throw(ArgumentError("k must be nonnegative, got $k"))
    ranked = sort!(collect(c.counts); by = kv -> (-kv.second, kv.first))
    return ranked[1:min(k, length(ranked))]
end

end

@testitem "basic operations and tie order" begin
    c = Counter{String}()
    for w in ["été", "日本", "été", "a", "b", "日本", "z"]
        add!(c, w)
    end
    @test c["été"] == 2 && c["nope"] == 0
    @test length(c) == 5 && total(c) == 7
    @test most_common(c, 3) == ["été" => 2, "日本" => 2, "a" => 1]
    @test most_common(c, 0) == []
    @test length(most_common(c, 99)) == 5
end

@testitem "remove! semantics" begin
    c = Counter{Int}()
    add!(c, 5, 3)
    remove!(c, 5, 2)
    @test c[5] == 1
    remove!(c, 5)
    @test length(c) == 0 && c[5] == 0
    @test_throws "only 0 present" remove!(c, 5)
    add!(c, 1, 2)
    @test_throws "cannot remove 3 of 1: only 2 present" remove!(c, 1, 3)
    @test_throws ArgumentError add!(c, 1, -1)
end

@testitem "random operations agree with a Dict model" begin
    using Random
    rng = MersenneTwister(1)
    c = Counter{Int}(); model = Dict{Int,Int}()
    bad = Ref{Any}(nothing)
    for step in 1:3000
        k = rand(rng, 1:8)
        if rand(rng) < 0.55
            n = rand(rng, 0:3); add!(c, k, n); n > 0 && (model[k] = get(model, k, 0) + n)
        else
            n = rand(rng, 0:3)
            if get(model, k, 0) >= n
                remove!(c, k, n)
                m = get(model, k, 0) - n
                m == 0 ? delete!(model, k) : (model[k] = m)
            else
                threw = try
                    remove!(c, k, n)
                    false
                catch e
                    e isa ArgumentError || rethrow()
                    true
                end
                threw || (bad[] = (:no_throw, step); break)
            end
        end
        expected = sort(collect(model); by = kv -> (-kv[2], kv[1]))
        (c.counts == model && most_common(c, 3) == expected[1:min(3, end)] && total(c) == sum(values(model); init = 0)) ||
            (bad[] = (step, c.counts, model); break)
    end
    @test isnothing(bad[])
end

module SafeDict

export LockedDict, update!, snapshot

struct LockedDict{K,V}
    data::Dict{K,V}
    lock::ReentrantLock
end
LockedDict{K,V}() where {K,V} = LockedDict{K,V}(Dict{K,V}(), ReentrantLock())

Base.get(d::LockedDict, key, default) = lock(() -> get(d.data, key, default), d.lock)
Base.length(d::LockedDict) = lock(() -> length(d.data), d.lock)
snapshot(d::LockedDict) = lock(() -> copy(d.data), d.lock)

function update!(f, d::LockedDict, key, default)
    old = get(d, key, default)
    new = f(old)
    lock(d.lock) do
        d.data[key] = new
    end
    return new
end

end

`LockedDict` and `update!` are in `/work/Project/SafeDict/src/SafeDict.jl`; all 9 test assertions pass.

The first run failed the concurrency test: after 8 tasks each did 200 increments the count was 235, not 1600. `update!` read the old value, released the lock, called `f` (which yields), and only then took the lock to write, so other tasks' updates were overwritten. The read, `f` and the write now happen inside one lock.

- 8 tasks x 200 increments of the same key, with an `f` that yields, give exactly 1600 and one key.

- A throwing `f` propagates and leaves the old value (5), and a later update gives 6.

arguments.content:
module QuantileLite

export percentile

function percentile(x::AbstractVector{<:Real}, p::Real)
    isempty(x) && throw(ArgumentError("cannot take a percentile of an empty vector"))
    0 <= p <= 1 || throw(ArgumentError("p must be in [0, 1], got $p"))
    any(isnan, x) && return float(eltype(x))(NaN)
    s = sort!(x)
    n = length(s)
    h = (n - 1) * p + 1
    lo = floor(Int, h)
    hi = min(lo + 1, n)
    T = float(eltype(x))
    return T(s[lo] + (h - lo) * (s[hi] - s[lo]))
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

module PolyEval

export polyval, polyder

function polyval(coeffs::AbstractVector, x)
    acc = zero(promote_type(eltype(coeffs), typeof(x)))
    for i in Iterators.reverse(eachindex(coeffs))
        acc = acc * x + coeffs[i]
    end
    return acc
end

function polyder(coeffs::AbstractVector)
    n = length(coeffs)
    n <= 1 && return [zero(eltype(coeffs))]
    return [(k - 1) * coeffs[firstindex(coeffs) + k - 1] for k in 2:n]
end

end

using TestItemRunner
@run_package_tests

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. module VarintCodec

export encode_varint, decode_varint

function encode_varint(n::UInt64)
    out = UInt8[]
    while n >= 0x80
        push!(out, UInt8(n & 0x7f) | 0x80)
        n >>= 7
    end
    push!(out, UInt8(n))
    return out
end

function decode_varint(bytes::AbstractVector{UInt8}, pos::Integer = firstindex(bytes))
    value = UInt64(0)
    for k in 0:9
        i = pos + k
        i <= lastindex(bytes) || throw(ArgumentError("truncated varint starting at position $pos"))
        b = bytes[i]
        value |= UInt64(b & 0x7f) << (7k)
        b < 0x80 && return value, i + 1
    end
    throw(ArgumentError("varint starting at position $pos is longer than 10 bytes"))
end

end

function.description: Run Julia test items and wait up to max_wait_seconds (default 600) for them to finish. This is the right way to run tests for a workspace that uses TestItems.jl — use it instead of shelling out to Pkg.test() or `julia --project -e`, which recompile everything and cannot report per-test results. Test items run in Julia worker processes that stay alive between calls and hot-reload edits via Revise, so repeat runs skip startup and most compilation. Runs every detected item when no filter is given; narrow with items, tags, name_pattern, file_pattern or package. Returns a summary plus one compact status line per item — failure messages, stack traces and captured output are deliberately omitted; call julia_get_testitem_detail with the ids you care about for those. All durations are milliseconds: per item, the time that item took; in the summary, elapsed wall-clock time for the whole run (not the sum of the per-item times, which overshoots because items run in parallel). Two independent time limits: `timeout` bounds each test item and errors the ones that exceed it; `max_wait_seconds` bounds this call only. When the wait runs out the run is NOT stopped — the response has status "running", the results so far and the testrun_id; poll julia_get_testrun_results until status is no longer "running", or stop the run with julia_cancel_testrun. A hanging test item (deadlock, blocking take!, infinite loop) therefore cannot hang this call, but it never finishes on its own either: if you suspect one, cancel and rerun with a `timeout` so that item is errored and the rest of the suite completes. If this call is interrupted or its result is lost, the run keeps going and its results stay retrievable — find the run with julia_list_testruns and fetch it with julia_get_testrun_results. Requires julia_set_workspace_folders.
function.name: mcp_julia_julia_run_testitems

timeout.description: Per-test-item time limit in seconds. An item still running when it expires is reported as errored (its message reads "timed out after N seconds"), its worker process is killed and replaced, and the rest of the run continues. No limit by default, so a hanging item runs until the run is cancelled — set this when a suite might hang or when every item must finish on its own. Unrelated to max_wait_seconds, which bounds this call rather than the items.

file_pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against file URIs.

max_workers.description: Maximum number of parallel test processes (default: the number of CPU threads, at most 8 and at most one per 3 GiB of system memory).

include_passing.description: List passing items too. Defaults to false — passing items are counted in the summary.

memory_threshold.description: Recycle a test worker once its own resident memory exceeds this fraction of total system memory, checked after each test item so no result is lost; the controller redistributes the worker's remaining items. Off by default. Use it for a suite whose workers grow run after run — note the fraction is of total memory, so on a large-memory machine a worth-recycling worker is still a small fraction.

mode.description: Execution mode (default "Normal"). Use "Coverage" to collect line coverage, then read it with julia_get_coverage_results.

tags.description: Filter to items carrying at least one of these tags.

max_wait_seconds.description: Longest this call blocks waiting for the run, in seconds (default 600). It returns as soon as the run finishes, so a large value costs nothing for a quick suite, and it never affects the run itself. If the run is still going when the wait expires, the response has status "running", the summary and per-item statuses so far and the testrun_id, and the run continues in the background: poll julia_get_testrun_results (each poll returns at once) or stop it with julia_cancel_testrun. Pass a smaller value if your client's tool-call limit is shorter; 0 starts the run and returns immediately.

function.description: Stop an in-progress Julia test run — typically one julia_run_testitems handed back with status "running" because it outlasted max_wait_seconds, or one that turned out to be hanging.
